Implementation Plan — Surface Agent Logs to the UI (Runner Parity with Muse Code)\n\n## Goal\n\nRestore the pre-runner (monolith) log experience now that agent execution has\nmoved to out-of-process runners. The UI should feel like watching Muse Code work\nlive, step by step, with full detail available as searchable history. This is a\nlog-fidelity and transport parity task, not a product change: no new AI\nsummaries, reuse existing structured log machinery.\n\n## Success Criteria (from the survey)\n\n- Live, step-by-step viewing of an agent running (Q1).\n- Always visible, using only data that already exists (Q2 + note \"don't use AI to generate summaries\"):\n  - short status updates,\n  - actions taken (files read/changed, commands run),\n  - full command/tool results,\n  - errors and retries,\n  - per-step timings.\n- The same detail available live and as history (Q3), i.e. full transparency.\n- Long-term retention, and the log must be searchable (Q4).\n- Secrets and PII are removed automatically before display, persistence, and any commit (Q5), because logs may land in the repository.\n- Existing gates stay green: `npm run test:unit`, `npm run lint`, focused log suites and headless screenshot checks.\n\n## Survey Constraints (binding)\n\nTaken from `SURVEY.md`:\n\n- Q1: \"Like watching it work live, step by step (Muse Code style)\".\n- Q2: all five detail classes; \"Only use things that already exist, don't use AI to generate summaries\".\n- Q3: \"Both live and history\" (\"Full transparency\").\n- Q4: \"Keep everything and make it searchable\".\n- Q5: \"Yes, hide secrets automatically\" plus PII, so committed logs stay safe.\n\n## Current-State Evidence (why fidelity was lost)\n\n### A. The structured pipeline already exists in-process\n\n- Normalized agent events are defined in `api/agent/sessionEvents.js` as\n  `AGENT_EVENT_NAMES`:\n  `run_started`, `assistant_delta`, `message_started`,\n  `tool_started`, `tool_updated`, `tool_finished`,\n  `run_finished`, `run_error`,\n  plus unified-log events\n  `usage_updated`, `session_meta`, `permission_requested`,\n  `permission_resolved`, `plan_updated`, `reasoning_delta`,\n  `harness_log`.\n- `api/agent/logStream/logProcessor.js` turns those events into canonical,\n  grouped records over feeds `main`, `thinking`, `tools`, `telemetry`, `raw`.\n- `api/agent/logStream/agentLogStreamer.js` wraps the processor and exposes\n  `handleEvent`, `system`, `consumeFeed`, `snapshot`, `renderText`,\n  `renderFeed`; `agentRunner.js` uses it in the embedded path and passes\n  entries through `onChunk`.\n- `api/watch/processLogs.js` renders legacy tags from structured entries,\n  synthesizes entries for system/GIT/CI/RUNNER lines, manages entry caps\n  (`_appendProcessLog`, `_appendLogEntries`, `_replaceLogEntries`,\n  `_capLogEntries`), and maps runner frames to kind `runner`.\n\n### B. The embedded path already preserves this\n\nIn `api/flow/execution/executeStage.js` (embedded mode), `agentRunner(...)`\nreceives `onChunk`; each chunk (`entry.text`) is appended via\n`_appendProcessLog` while running, and after the stage\n`_replaceLogEntries(task, startIndex, result.logEntries)` upgrades the\nsynthesized entries to the streamer's structured entries. The candidate\nUI then receives everything through `adaptTaskEntries` in\n`frontend/src/components/tasks/LogsPanel.jsx` -> `LogViewer`.\n\n### C. The runner boundary only carries text — this is the regression\n\n- `runner/harness.js::runHarnessStage` subscribes to the session but forwards\n  only:\n  - `assistant_delta.delta` as `event.delta`\n  - `harness_log.text` as `event.text`,\n  and only those two. It drops `tool_started/updated/finished` (args, full\n  results, timings), `reasoning_delta`, `usage_updated`, `permission_*`,\n  `plan_updated`, and structured error/retry data. It returns only `output`.\n- `runner/daemon.js` turns any `onLog(text)` call into newline-split chunks via\n  `sendLogs`, each POSTed to `/tasks/:id/logs` with `bytes` only.\n- `api/flow/executionLedger.js::ingestLogs` treats each frame as a text string\n  and calls `_appendProcessLog(task, \\`[runner ${runnerId}] ${bytes}\\`, ...)`.\n  That is why the UI only sees runner-prefixed text chunks instead of\n  `[TOOL]`/`[RESULT]`/`[THINKING]`/telemetry records with args and timings.\n- `api/flow/execution/applyRunnerReport.js` persists `outcome.output`\n  (final assistant text) into the stage report and uses it as\n  `streamedOutput`; it does not restore tool, thinking, usage, or timing\n  entries. (Exit-code/output tail behavior is retained.)\n- `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js::/tasks/:id/logs` additionally emits a\n  `process:stdout` socket event limited to the runner-prefixed text chunk,\n  so the live tail matches the coarse ingest.\n\n### D. UI already has the viewer we need\n\n- `frontend/src/components/logs/` contains `LogViewer.jsx`, `adapters.js`,\n  `logCategories.js`, `logViewerState.js` with category chips, search, density,\n  timestamps, grouped expandable rows, and follow-scroll. The task surface\n  calls `useTaskLogs` -> `adaptTaskEntries`.\n- `shared/toolLogFormat/` contains `summarizeToolStart`, `summarizeToolResult`,\n  `summarizeUsage`, `summarizePermission`, `summarizePlan`, `stripAnsi`, plus\n  normalization/truncation helpers. This is the canonical formatter; do not\n  duplicate it.\n- Redaction today is environment-variable-name based only:\n  `api/agent/harnesses/shared/harnessScaffold.js` exports\n  `SECRET_NAME_PATTERN`, used to drop secret-shaped env vars from child envs.\n  There is no content/PII redactor for log text; one must be introduced.\n- Caps: `config.logEntriesMaxCount` defaults to 500 (from schema/tests).\n  Survey Q4 (\"keep everything\") conflicts with the current eviction policy and\n  needs an explicit decision (pagination/archive, not silent truncation).\n\n## Principle used throughout\n\nMake change easy first (refactors, redaction choke point, structured transport\nplumbing with no behavior change), then make the change (widen forwarding,\npersist/stream everything, render everything). Research that decides the shape\nof the work comes before coding changes.\n\n## Phase 0 — Research first (big unknowns; no behavior change)\n\n- R1 Runner->backend log path audit (done largely above; finalize exact\n  client contract): confirm `runner/client.js::logs` payload constraints,\n  batching, retry, and whether a structured-event upload is viable or requires\n  a new endpoint/field. Output: event-coverage matrix with rows = 17\n  normalized AGENT_EVENT_NAMES and runner columns `forward`,\n  `preserve order`, `backend ingest`, `live socket`, `persisted`,\n  `UI render`; mark current-state pass/drop, and the target state every row\n  must reach.\n- R2 Backend->UI/live path audit: map `api/routes/ws.js`, `api/eventBridge.js`,\n  `api/routes/sessions.js`, task log endpoints, `useWebSocket`, `useTaskLogs`,\n  `adaptTaskEntries`, `fullTextIndex`, and `normalizeEntries`. Confirm (a)\n  whether WS delivers structured entries or only process lines, (b) what the\n  logs tab refetches after run completion, and (c) how history is retained\n  and capped. Output: second half of coverage matrix + retention limits.\n- R3 Redaction inventory and chosen home:\n  - reuse `SECRET_NAME_PATTERN` for env-var-name secrets;\n  - add a content redactor for tokens, keys, passwords, bearer/basic\n    headers, connection strings, cloud credential JSON, PII (emails, user\n    paths, phone/card-like), with evidence on whether each category is\n    already detected somewhere (no: only env-name patterns exist);\n  - choose `logRecord.js`/`logProcessor.js` as the choke point so all sources\n    (embedded agent, runner ingest, command stages, git/ci) share one\n    redactor, and document allow-list assumptions.\n- R4 Retention and search feasibility:\n  - evaluate `logEntriesMaxCount`/lane budgets against \"keep everything\";\n  - propose retention model: raised cap + bounded lane budgets, client-side\n    full-text search retained, with optional paged history beyond cap via\n    execution-archive only if volume demands;\n  - keep the eviction marker contract intact.\n- R5 (small) confirmation of runner UI category wiring: inspect whether the\n  smoothness issue is caused only by coarse runner chunks, or additionally by\n  monitor surfaces that exclude tool mirrors. Output: call sites and chips.\n- Gate: append the finalized coverage matrix + decisions to this file before\n  changing behavior. If R1-R4 contradict the plan below, revise first.\n\n## Phase 1 — Make the change easy (refactors, no behavior change)\n\n- E1 Freeze the parity contract.\n  - Add/extend a contract test in `api/agent/logStream/harnessFidelity.test.js`\n    (or sibling) that asserts every `AGENT_EVENT_NAMES` entry maps to a\n    structured record + feed + rendered tag, and captures failing rows as the\n    acceptance checklist. No producer change yet.\n- E2 Single redaction choke point.\n  - Introduce one redaction helper (new module under `shared/` or `api/watch/`\n    per R3, no duplication), applied inside `logRecord.js`/`logProcessor.js`\n    at record creation, and inside runner ingest and `applyRunnerReport` for\n    any text passed through.\n  - Wire into the embedded path; verify byte-identical behavior on clean\n    inputs (all existing tests green) by covering redaction fixtures.\n- E3 Runner plumbing for structured events without changing current behavior.\n  - Refactor `runHarnessStage` subscription to an `onEvent(event)` structured\n    callback, deriving `onLog(text)` for backwards compatibility. Add\n    optional structured upload hooks, keeping existing text behavior as a\n    fallback.\n  - Unit-test that existing callers receive byte-identical text output.\n- E4 Structured ingest in backend, optional and backward-compatible.\n  - Extend `/tasks/:id/logs` or add `/tasks/:id/log-events` (R1 decision) so a\n    runner can send structured event batches; `executionLedger` forwards them\n    to `_appendLogEntries`/`_replaceLogEntries`-style handling, preserves seq\n    ordering and gap/duplicate semantics, while still falling back to prefixed\n    text for old runners.\n\n## Phase 2 — Make the change (restore fidelity)\n\n- C1 Runner forwards everything.\n  - Change `runHarnessStage` and daemon sending to forward all normalized\n    events with payload (tool args, tool result partials/finals, thinking\n    deltas, usage, permissions, plan updates, session meta, errors/retries)\n    and timing data derived from event processing.\n  - Preserve runner-generated `seq` ordering across batches and retries.\n  - Redact on the sending side too, in case a runner runs locally and reads\n    local secret-bearing output.\n- C2 Backend persists and streams everything.\n  - Route runner events through `agentLogStreamer`/`logProcessor` (or the same\n    structured ingest path as E4) into `task.logEntries`.\n  - Raise/justify retention caps per R4; never silently drop events except\n    under the existing eviction marker.\n  - Push the same events to live WS channel with structured entry shape, not\n    only the `[runner ...]` text line; keep that text line as one legacy view.\n  - Ensure `applyRunnerReport` receives/stores structured `logEntries`\n    (or preserves the ingested ones) and passes final output separately.\n- C3 UI renders everything live and as history.\n  - Ensure `adaptTaskEntry` and `adaptProcessLogLine` preserve tags/kind/tool\n    fields, timing fields, and expandable detail.\n  - Add/enable categories for tool arguments, tool results, thinking,\n    errors/retries, permissions, plan updates, telemetry, raw evidence in\n    `LogViewer`.\n  - Live append must remain incremental with follow-scroll; follow-scroll\n    restoration on tab return must still work.\n  - History view must refetch complete retained log and keep client-side\n    searching; confirm search finds tool names, command names, error text.\n- C4 \"Keep everything, searchable\" + secret/PII safety.\n  - Implement R4 retention (cap changes + lane budgets + pagination/virtual\n    scroll if needed), keeping eviction markers for units beyond cap.\n  - Add test proving a secret in a tool result never reaches `task.logEntries`,\n    live WS payload, task docs committed, or report persisted output tail.\n  - Cover PII shape fixtures from R3.\n\n## Phase 3 — Assurance (testing + documentation)\n\n- T1 Contract + unit tests (primary gate `npm run test:unit`):\n  - parity contract from E1 fully green;\n  - redaction tests for env-name secrets, Inline key/value, bearer/basic,\n    connection strings, cloud credentials, PII (email/user path/phone/card)\n    plus clean-input passthrough;\n  - runner forwarding/ordering tests;\n  - executionLedger structured ingest tests including seq gaps/duplicates;\n  - adapter/category tests for every feed/kind.\n- T2 Integration tests:\n  - runner->backend->WS round-trip asserting a tool call with args/result,\n    an error/retry, and a timing record arrive live and persist as history;\n  - history fetch/search across completed runs;\n  - applyRunnerReport keeps structured entries and report detail.\n- T3 UI verification:\n  - use existing `LogViewer` unit tests + fixture data for all categories,\n    timestamps, density, search, expand/collapse, follow-scroll;\n  - visual only via `npm run capture:screenshot` against existing\n    fixtures/mocks if needed; no bespoke long-lived servers.\n- T4 Gates before completion:\n  - `npm run test:unit` (must pass),\n  - `npm run lint` (must pass),\n  - `npm run docs:check` if documentation content is changed.\n  Record commands and results in the stage/final report.\n- D1 Documentation:\n  - short section describing what is logged, live/history behavior, retention\n    and search, redaction guarantee, ordering/gap behavior, and residual\n    unknown-secret risk (report-a-secret path);\n  - keep it linked from existing task/activity docs rather than duplicating\n    contract text.\n- D2 Appendix:\n  - final coverage matrix with all rows passing;\n  - explicit non-goals (no AI summaries, no new transport, no new formatter,\n    no server-side full-text search unless R4 proves client-side insufficient).\n\n## Validation Plan\n\n- Primary gate: `npm run test:unit`.\n- Secondary: `npm run lint`, and `npm run docs:check` once D1 lands.\n- Focused suites: `api/agent/logStream/*.test.js`, `api/flow/runnerRoutes.test.js`,\n  runner tests, `frontend/src/components/logs/*`.\n- Manual/headless: open a task using a mock log fixture and verify\n  step-by-step live appends (assistant text, assistant reasoning, tool call\n  with args, tool result, error/retry, usage, permission/plan), timings, then\n  reload and confirm identical history, search for a tool name, and confirm a\n  secret/PII is absent from store/WS/report via tests. Use\n  `npm run capture:screenshot` only if a visual concern remains.\n\n## Risks and Mitigations\n\n- Volume vs. \"keep everything\": mitigate with pagination/virtual scroll and\n  lane budgets, not narrative truncation.\n- Ordering across runner->backend->WS and retries: pin a seq/timestamp\n  contract in the new structured ingest and integration-test it.\n- Unknown secret shapes: redactor starts from R3 inventory + common patterns;\n  document residual risk and report-a-secret path.\n- Secret-safe by position: redact before persistence and before commits;\n  tests cover store, WS, and report paths.\n- Backwards compatibility: text ingest (`/tasks/:id/logs`) remains usable,\n  so older runners degrade only to the current coarse text view rather than\n  failure.\n\n## Phase 0 Findings (research gate — completed before behavior changes)\n\n- R1 Runner->backend contract: `runner/client.js::logs` posts `{seq, bytes}`;\n  structured transport added as `POST /tasks/:id/log-events` with\n  `{seq, events[1..200]}` (400 otherwise). Structured batches ride a new\n  `process:log-entries`/`PROCESS_LOG_ENTRIES` frame into the same array as\n  attached `.entry` records, so stored/live dedupe is unchanged. Implementation Plan — Surface Agent Logs to the UI (Runner Parity with Muse Code)\n\n## Goal\n\nRestore the pre-runner (monolith) log experience now that agent execution has\nmoved to out-of-process runners. The UI should feel like watching Muse Code work\nlive, step by step, with full detail available as searchable history. This is a\nlog-fidelity and transport parity task, not a product change: no new AI\nsummaries, reuse existing structured log machinery.\n\n## Success Criteria (from the survey)\n\n- Live, step-by-step viewing of an agent running (Q1).\n- Always visible, using only data that already exists (Q2 + note \"don't use AI to generate summaries\"):\n  - short status updates,\n  - actions taken (files read/changed, commands run),\n  - full command/tool results,\n  - errors and retries,\n  - per-step timings.\n- The same detail available live and as history (Q3), i.e. full transparency.\n- Long-term retention, and the log must be searchable (Q4).\n- Secrets and PII are removed automatically before display, persistence, and any commit (Q5), because logs may land in the repository.\n- Existing gates stay green: `npm run test:unit`, `npm run lint`, focused log suites and headless screenshot checks.\n\n## Survey Constraints (binding)\n\nTaken from `SURVEY.md`:\n\n- Q1: \"Like watching it work live, step by step (Muse Code style)\".\n- Q2: all five detail classes; \"Only use things that already exist, don't use AI to generate summaries\".\n- Q3: \"Both live and history\" (\"Full transparency\").\n- Q4: \"Keep everything and make it searchable\".\n- Q5: \"Yes, hide secrets automatically\" plus PII, so committed logs stay safe.\n\n## Current-State Evidence (why fidelity was lost)\n\n### A. The structured pipeline already exists in-process\n\n- Normalized agent events are defined in `api/agent/sessionEvents.js` as\n  `AGENT_EVENT_NAMES`:\n  `run_started`, `assistant_delta`, `message_started`,\n  `tool_started`, `tool_updated`, `tool_finished`,\n  `run_finished`, `run_error`,\n  plus unified-log events\n  `usage_updated`, `session_meta`, `permission_requested`,\n  `permission_resolved`, `plan_updated`, `reasoning_delta`,\n  `harness_log`.\n- `api/agent/logStream/logProcessor.js` turns those events into canonical,\n  grouped records over feeds `main`, `thinking`, `tools`, `telemetry`, `raw`.\n- `api/agent/logStream/agentLogStreamer.js` wraps the processor and exposes\n  `handleEvent`, `system`, `consumeFeed`, `snapshot`, `renderText`,\n  `renderFeed`; `agentRunner.js` uses it in the embedded path and passes\n  entries through `onChunk`.\n- `api/watch/processLogs.js` renders legacy tags from structured entries,\n  synthesizes entries for system/GIT/CI/RUNNER lines, manages entry caps\n  (`_appendProcessLog`, `_appendLogEntries`, `_replaceLogEntries`,\n  `_capLogEntries`), and maps runner frames to kind `runner`.\n\n### B. The embedded path already preserves this\n\nIn `api/flow/execution/executeStage.js` (embedded mode), `agentRunner(...)`\nreceives `onChunk`; each chunk (`entry.text`) is appended via\n`_appendProcessLog` while running, and after the stage\n`_replaceLogEntries(task, startIndex, result.logEntries)` upgrades the\nsynthesized entries to the streamer's structured entries. The candidate\nUI then receives everything through `adaptTaskEntries` in\n`frontend/src/components/tasks/LogsPanel.jsx` -> `LogViewer`.\n\n### C. The runner boundary only carries text — this is the regression\n\n- `runner/harness.js::runHarnessStage` subscribes to the session but forwards\n  only:\n  - `assistant_delta.delta` as `event.delta`\n  - `harness_log.text` as `event.text`,\n  and only those two. It drops `tool_started/updated/finished` (args, full\n  results, timings), `reasoning_delta`, `usage_updated`, `permission_*`,\n  `plan_updated`, and structured error/retry data. It returns only `output`.\n- `runner/daemon.js` turns any `onLog(text)` call into newline-split chunks via\n  `sendLogs`, each POSTed to `/tasks/:id/logs` with `bytes` only.\n- `api/flow/executionLedger.js::ingestLogs` treats each frame as a text string\n  and calls `_appendProcessLog(task, \\`[runner ${runnerId}] ${bytes}\\`, ...)`.\n  That is why the UI only sees runner-prefixed text chunks instead of\n  `[TOOL]`/`[RESULT]`/`[THINKING]`/telemetry records with args and timings.\n- `api/flow/execution/applyRunnerReport.js` persists `outcome.output`\n  (final assistant text) into the stage report and uses it as\n  `streamedOutput`; it does not restore tool, thinking, usage, or timing\n  entries. (Exit-code/output tail behavior is retained.)\n- `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js::/tasks/:id/logs` additionally emits a\n  `process:stdout` socket event limited to the runner-prefixed text chunk,\n  so the live tail matches the coarse ingest.\n\n### D. UI already has the viewer we need\n\n- `frontend/src/components/logs/` contains `LogViewer.jsx`, `adapters.js`,\n  `logCategories.js`, `logViewerState.js` with category chips, search, density,\n  timestamps, grouped expandable rows, and follow-scroll. The task surface\n  calls `useTaskLogs` -> `adaptTaskEntries`.\n- `shared/toolLogFormat/` contains `summarizeToolStart`, `summarizeToolResult`,\n  `summarizeUsage`, `summarizePermission`, `summarizePlan`, `stripAnsi`, plus\n  normalization/truncation helpers. This is the canonical formatter; do not\n  duplicate it.\n- Redaction today is environment-variable-name based only:\n  `api/agent/harnesses/shared/harnessScaffold.js` exports\n  `SECRET_NAME_PATTERN`, used to drop secret-shaped env vars from child envs.\n  There is no content/PII redactor for log text; one must be introduced.\n- Caps: `config.logEntriesMaxCount` defaults to 500 (from schema/tests).\n  Survey Q4 (\"keep everything\") conflicts with the current eviction policy and\n  needs an explicit decision (pagination/archive, not silent truncation).\n\n## Principle used throughout\n\nMake change easy first (refactors, redaction choke point, structured transport\nplumbing with no behavior change), then make the change (widen forwarding,\npersist/stream everything, render everything). Research that decides the shape\nof the work comes before coding changes.\n\n## Phase 0 — Research first (big unknowns; no behavior change)\n\n- R1 Runner->backend log path audit (done largely above; finalize exact\n  client contract): confirm `runner/client.js::logs` payload constraints,\n  batching, retry, and whether a structured-event upload is viable or requires\n  a new endpoint/field. Output: event-coverage matrix with rows = 17\n  normalized AGENT_EVENT_NAMES and runner columns `forward`,\n  `preserve order`, `backend ingest`, `live socket`, `persisted`,\n  `UI render`; mark current-state pass/drop, and the target state every row\n  must reach.\n- R2 Backend->UI/live path audit: map `api/routes/ws.js`, `api/eventBridge.js`,\n  `api/routes/sessions.js`, task log endpoints, `useWebSocket`, `useTaskLogs`,\n  `adaptTaskEntries`, `fullTextIndex`, and `normalizeEntries`. Confirm (a)\n  whether WS delivers structured entries or only process lines, (b) what the\n  logs tab refetches after run completion, and (c) how history is retained\n  and capped. Output: second half of coverage matrix + retention limits.\n- R3 Redaction inventory and chosen home:\n  - reuse `SECRET_NAME_PATTERN` for env-var-name secrets;\n  - add a content redactor for tokens, keys, passwords, bearer/basic\n    headers, connection strings, cloud credential JSON, PII (emails, user\n    paths, phone/card-like), with evidence on whether each category is\n    already detected somewhere (no: only env-name patterns exist);\n  - choose `logRecord.js`/`logProcessor.js` as the choke point so all sources\n    (embedded agent, runner ingest, command stages, git/ci) share one\n    redactor, and document allow-list assumptions.\n- R4 Retention and search feasibility:\n  - evaluate `logEntriesMaxCount`/lane budgets against \"keep everything\";\n  - propose retention model: raised cap + bounded lane budgets, client-side\n    full-text search retained, with optional paged history beyond cap via\n    execution-archive only if volume demands;\n  - keep the eviction marker contract intact.\n- R5 (small) confirmation of runner UI category wiring: inspect whether the\n  smoothness issue is caused only by coarse runner chunks, or additionally by\n  monitor surfaces that exclude tool mirrors. Output: call sites and chips.\n- Gate: append the finalized coverage matrix + decisions to this file before\n  changing behavior. If R1-R4 contradict the plan below, revise first.\n\n## Phase 1 — Make the change easy (refactors, no behavior change)\n\n- E1 Freeze the parity contract.\n  - Add/extend a contract test in `api/agent/logStream/harnessFidelity.test.js`\n    (or sibling) that asserts every `AGENT_EVENT_NAMES` entry maps to a\n    structured record + feed + rendered tag, and captures failing rows as the\n    acceptance checklist. No producer change yet.\n- E2 Single redaction choke point.\n  - Introduce one redaction helper (new module under `shared/` or `api/watch/`\n    per R3, no duplication), applied inside `logRecord.js`/`logProcessor.js`\n    at record creation, and inside runner ingest and `applyRunnerReport` for\n    any text passed through.\n  - Wire into the embedded path; verify byte-identical behavior on clean\n    inputs (all existing tests green) by covering redaction fixtures.\n- E3 Runner plumbing for structured events without changing current behavior.\n  - Refactor `runHarnessStage` subscription to an `onEvent(event)` structured\n    callback, deriving `onLog(text)` for backwards compatibility. Add\n    optional structured upload hooks, keeping existing text behavior as a\n    fallback.\n  - Unit-test that existing callers receive byte-identical text output.\n- E4 Structured ingest in backend, optional and backward-compatible.\n  - Extend `/tasks/:id/logs` or add `/tasks/:id/log-events` (R1 decision) so a\n    runner can send structured event batches; `executionLedger` forwards them\n    to `_appendLogEntries`/`_replaceLogEntries`-style handling, preserves seq\n    ordering and gap/duplicate semantics, while still falling back to prefixed\n    text for old runners.\n\n## Phase 2 — Make the change (restore fidelity)\n\n- C1 Runner forwards everything.\n  - Change `runHarnessStage` and daemon sending to forward all normalized\n    events with payload (tool args, tool result partials/finals, thinking\n    deltas, usage, permissions, plan updates, session meta, errors/retries)\n    and timing data derived from event processing.\n  - Preserve runner-generated `seq` ordering across batches and retries.\n  - Redact on the sending side too, in case a runner runs locally and reads\n    local secret-bearing output.\n- C2 Backend persists and streams everything.\n  - Route runner events through `agentLogStreamer`/`logProcessor` (or the same\n    structured ingest path as E4) into `task.logEntries`.\n  - Raise/justify retention caps per R4; never silently drop events except\n    under the existing eviction marker.\n  - Push the same events to live WS channel with structured entry shape, not\n    only the `[runner ...]` text line; keep that text line as one legacy view.\n  - Ensure `applyRunnerReport` receives/stores structured `logEntries`\n    (or preserves the ingested ones) and passes final output separately.\n- C3 UI renders everything live and as history.\n  - Ensure `adaptTaskEntry` and `adaptProcessLogLine` preserve tags/kind/tool\n    fields, timing fields, and expandable detail.\n  - Add/enable categories for tool arguments, tool results, thinking,\n    errors/retries, permissions, plan updates, telemetry, raw evidence in\n    `LogViewer`.\n  - Live append must remain incremental with follow-scroll; follow-scroll\n    restoration on tab return must still work.\n  - History view must refetch complete retained log and keep client-side\n    searching; confirm search finds tool names, command names, error text.\n- C4 \"Keep everything, searchable\" + secret/PII safety.\n  - Implement R4 retention (cap changes + lane budgets + pagination/virtual\n    scroll if needed), keeping eviction markers for units beyond cap.\n  - Add test proving a secret in a tool result never reaches `task.logEntries`,\n    live WS payload, task docs committed, or report persisted output tail.\n  - Cover PII shape fixtures from R3.\n\n## Phase 3 — Assurance (testing + documentation)\n\n- T1 Contract + unit tests (primary gate `npm run test:unit`):\n  - parity contract from E1 fully green;\n  - redaction tests for env-name secrets, Inline key/value, bearer/basic,\n    connection strings, cloud credentials, PII (email/user path/phone/card)\n    plus clean-input passthrough;\n  - runner forwarding/ordering tests;\n  - executionLedger structured ingest tests including seq gaps/duplicates;\n  - adapter/category tests for every feed/kind.\n- T2 Integration tests:\n  - runner->backend->WS round-trip asserting a tool call with args/result,\n    an error/retry, and a timing record arrive live and persist as history;\n  - history fetch/search across completed runs;\n  - applyRunnerReport keeps structured entries and report detail.\n- T3 UI verification:\n  - use existing `LogViewer` unit tests + fixture data for all categories,\n    timestamps, density, search, expand/collapse, follow-scroll;\n  - visual only via `npm run capture:screenshot` against existing\n    fixtures/mocks if needed; no bespoke long-lived servers.\n- T4 Gates before completion:\n  - `npm run test:unit` (must pass),\n  - `npm run lint` (must pass),\n  - `npm run docs:check` if documentation content is changed.\n  Record commands and results in the stage/final report.\n- D1 Documentation:\n  - short section describing what is logged, live/history behavior, retention\n    and search, redaction guarantee, ordering/gap behavior, and residual\n    unknown-secret risk (report-a-secret path);\n  - keep it linked from existing task/activity docs rather than duplicating\n    contract text.\n- D2 Appendix:\n  - final coverage matrix with all rows passing;\n  - explicit non-goals (no AI summaries, no new transport, no new formatter,\n    no server-side full-text search unless R4 proves client-side insufficient).\n\n## Validation Plan\n\n- Primary gate: `npm run test:unit`.\n- Secondary: `npm run lint`, and `npm run docs:check` once D1 lands.\n- Focused suites: `api/agent/logStream/*.test.js`, `api/flow/runnerRoutes.test.js`,\n  runner tests, `frontend/src/components/logs/*`.\n- Manual/headless: open a task using a mock log fixture and verify\n  step-by-step live appends (assistant text, assistant reasoning, tool call\n  with args, tool result, error/retry, usage, permission/plan), timings, then\n  reload and confirm identical history, search for a tool name, and confirm a\n  secret/PII is absent from store/WS/report via tests. Use\n  `npm run capture:screenshot` only if a visual concern remains.\n\n## Risks and Mitigations\n\n- Volume vs. \"keep everything\": mitigate with pagination/virtual scroll and\n  lane budgets, not narrative truncation.\n- Ordering across runner->backend->WS and retries: pin a seq/timestamp\n  contract in the new structured ingest and integration-test it.\n- Unknown secret shapes: redactor starts from R3 inventory + common patterns;\n  document residual risk and report-a-secret path.\n- Secret-safe by position: redact before persistence and before commits;\n  tests cover store, WS, and report paths.\n- Backwards compatibility: text ingest (`/tasks/:id/logs`) remains usable,\n  so older runners degrade only to the current coarse text view rather than\n  failure.\n\n## Phase 0 Findings (research gate — completed before behavior changes)\n\n- R1 Runner->backend contract: `runner/client.js::logs` posts `{seq, bytes}`;\n  structured transport added as `POST /tasks/:id/log-events` with\n  `{seq, events[1..200]}` (400 otherwise). The candidate\nUI then receives everything through `adaptTaskEntries` in\n`frontend/src/components/tasks/LogsPanel.jsx` -> `LogViewer`.\n\n### C. The runner boundary only carries text — this is the regression\n\n- `runner/harness.js::runHarnessStage` subscribes to the session but forwards\n  only:\n  - `assistant_delta.delta` as `event.delta`\n  - `harness_log.text` as `event.text`,\n  and only those two. It drops `tool_started/updated/finished` (args, full\n  results, timings), `reasoning_delta`, `usage_updated`, `permission_*`,\n  `plan_updated`, and structured error/retry data. It returns only `output`.\n- `runner/daemon.js` turns any `onLog(text)` call into newline-split chunks via\n  `sendLogs`, each POSTed to `/tasks/:id/logs` with `bytes` only.\n- `api/flow/executionLedger.js::ingestLogs` treats each frame as a text string\n  and calls `_appendProcessLog(task, \\`[runner ${runnerId}] ${bytes}\\`, ...)`.\n  That is why the UI only sees runner-prefixed text chunks instead of\n  `[TOOL]`/`[RESULT]`/`[THINKING]`/telemetry records with args and timings.\n- `api/flow/execution/applyRunnerReport.js` persists `outcome.output`\n  (final assistant text) into the stage report and uses it as\n  `streamedOutput`; it does not restore tool, thinking, usage, or timing\n  entries. (Exit-code/output tail behavior is retained.)\n- `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js::/tasks/:id/logs` additionally emits a\n  `process:stdout` socket event limited to the runner-prefixed text chunk,\n  so the live tail matches the coarse ingest.\n\n### D. UI already has the viewer we need\n\n- `frontend/src/components/logs/` contains `LogViewer.jsx`, `adapters.js`,\n  `logCategories.js`, `logViewerState.js` with category chips, search, density,\n  timestamps, grouped expandable rows, and follow-scroll. The task surface\n  calls `useTaskLogs` -> `adaptTaskEntries`.\n- `shared/toolLogFormat/` contains `summarizeToolStart`, `summarizeToolResult`,\n  `summarizeUsage`, `summarizePermission`, `summarizePlan`, `stripAnsi`, plus\n  normalization/truncation helpers. This is the canonical formatter; do not\n  duplicate it.\n- Redaction today is environment-variable-name based only:\n  `api/agent/harnesses/shared/harnessScaffold.js` exports\n  `SECRET_NAME_PATTERN`, used to drop secret-shaped env vars from child envs.\n  There is no content/PII redactor for log text; one must be introduced.\n- Caps: `config.logEntriesMaxCount` defaults to 500 (from schema/tests).\n  Survey Q4 (\"keep everything\") conflicts with the current eviction policy and\n  needs an explicit decision (pagination/archive, not silent truncation).\n\n## Principle used throughout\n\nMake change easy first (refactors, redaction choke point, structured transport\nplumbing with no behavior change), then make the change (widen forwarding,\npersist/stream everything, render everything). `executionLedger` forwards them\n    to `_appendLogEntries`/`_replaceLogEntries`-style handling, preserves seq\n    ordering and gap/duplicate semantics, while still falling back to prefixed\n    text for old runners.\n\n## Phase 2 — Make the change (restore fidelity)\n\n- C1 Runner forwards everything.\n  - Change `runHarnessStage` and daemon sending to forward all normalized\n    events with payload (tool args, tool result partials/finals, thinking\n    deltas, usage, permissions, plan updates, session meta, errors/retries)\n    and timing data derived from event processing.\n  - Preserve runner-generated `seq` ordering across batches and retries.\n  - Redact on the sending side too, in case a runner runs locally and reads\n    local secret-bearing output.\n- C2 Backend persists and streams everything.\n  - Route runner events through `agentLogStreamer`/`logProcessor` (or the same\n    structured ingest path as E4) into `task.logEntries`.\n  - Raise/justify retention caps per R4; No producer change yet.\n- E2 Single redaction choke point.\n  - Introduce one redaction helper (new module under `shared/` or `api/watch/`\n    per R3, no duplication), applied inside `logRecord.js`/`logProcessor.js`\n    at record creation, and inside runner ingest and `applyRunnerReport` for\n    any text passed through.\n  - Wire into the embedded path; verify byte-identical behavior on clean\n    inputs (all existing tests green) by covering redaction fixtures.\n- E3 Runner plumbing for structured events without changing current behavior.\n  - Refactor `runHarnessStage` subscription to an `onEvent(event)` structured\n    callback, deriving `onLog(text)` for backwards compatibility. Implementation Plan — Surface Agent Logs to the UI (Runner Parity with Muse Code)\\n\\n## Goal\\n\\nRestore the pre-runner (monolith) log experience now that agent execution has\\nmoved to out-of-process runners. The UI should feel like watching Muse Code work\\nlive, step by step, with full detail available as searchable history. This is a\\nlog-fidelity and transport parity task, not a product change: no new AI\\nsummaries, reuse existing structured log machinery.\\n\\n## Success Criteria (from the survey)\\n\\n- Live, step-by-step viewing of an agent running (Q1).\\n- Always visible, using only data that already exists (Q2 + note \\\"don't use AI to generate summaries\\\"):\\n  - short status updates,\\n  - actions taken (files read/changed, commands run),\\n  - full command/tool results,\\n  - errors and retries,\\n  - per-step timings.\\n- The same detail available live and as history (Q3), i.e. full transparency.\\n- Long-term retention, and the log must be searchable (Q4).\\n- Secrets and PII are removed automatically before display, persistence, and any commit (Q5), because logs may land in the repository.\\n- Existing gates stay green: `npm run test:unit`, `npm run lint`, focused log suites and headless screenshot checks.\\n\\n## Survey Constraints (binding)\\n\\nTaken from `SURVEY.md`:\\n\\n- Q1: \\\"Like watching it work live, step by step (Muse Code style)\\\".\\n- Q2: all five detail classes; \\\"Only use things that already exist, don't use AI to generate summaries\\\".\\n- Q3: \\\"Both live and history\\\" (\\\"Full transparency\\\").\\n- Q4: \\\"Keep everything and make it searchable\\\".\\n- Q5: \\\"Yes, hide secrets automatically\\\" plus PII, so committed logs stay safe.\\n\\n## Current-State Evidence (why fidelity was lost)\\n\\n### A. The structured pipeline already exists in-process\\n\\n- Normalized agent events are defined in `api/agent/sessionEvents.js` as\\n  `AGENT_EVENT_NAMES`:\\n  `run_started`, `assistant_delta`, `message_started`,\\n  `tool_started`, `tool_updated`, `tool_finished`,\\n  `run_finished`, `run_error`,\\n  plus unified-log events\\n  `usage_updated`, `session_meta`, `permission_requested`,\\n  `permission_resolved`, `plan_updated`, `reasoning_delta`,\\n  `harness_log`.\\n- `api/agent/logStream/logProcessor.js` turns those events into canonical,\\n  grouped records over feeds `main`, `thinking`, `tools`, `telemetry`, `raw`.\\n- `api/agent/logStream/agentLogStreamer.js` wraps the processor and exposes\\n  `handleEvent`, `system`, `consumeFeed`, `snapshot`, `renderText`,\\n  `renderFeed`; `agentRunner.js` uses it in the embedded path and passes\\n  entries through `onChunk`.\\n- `api/watch/processLogs.js` renders legacy tags from structured entries,\\n  synthesizes entries for system/GIT/CI/RUNNER lines, manages entry caps\\n  (`_appendProcessLog`, `_appendLogEntries`, `_replaceLogEntries`,\\n  `_capLogEntries`), and maps runner frames to kind `runner`.\\n\\n### B. The embedded path already preserves this\\n\\nIn `api/flow/execution/executeStage.js` (embedded mode), `agentRunner(...)`\\nreceives `onChunk`; each chunk (`entry.text`) is appended via\\n`_appendProcessLog` while running, and after the stage\\n`_replaceLogEntries(task, startIndex, result.logEntries)` upgrades the\\nsynthesized entries to the streamer's structured entries. The candidate\\nUI then receives everything through `adaptTaskEntries` in\\n`frontend/src/components/tasks/LogsPanel.jsx` -> `LogViewer`.\\n\\n### C. The runner boundary only carries text — this is the regression\\n\\n- `runner/harness.js::runHarnessStage` subscribes to the session but forwards\\n  only:\\n  - `assistant_delta.delta` as `event.delta`\\n  - `harness_log.text` as `event.text`,\\n  and only those two. It drops `tool_started/updated/finished` (args, full\\n  results, timings), `reasoning_delta`, `usage_updated`, `permission_*`,\\n  `plan_updated`, and structured error/retry data. It returns only `output`.\\n- `runner/daemon.js` turns any `onLog(text)` call into newline-split chunks via\\n  `sendLogs`, each POSTed to `/tasks/:id/logs` with `bytes` only.\\n- `api/flow/executionLedger.js::ingestLogs` treats each frame as a text string\\n  and calls `_appendProcessLog(task, \\\\`[runner ${runnerId}] ${bytes}\\\\`, ...)`.\\n  That is why the UI only sees runner-prefixed text chunks instead of\\n  `[TOOL]`/`[RESULT]`/`[THINKING]`/telemetry records with args and timings.\\n- `api/flow/execution/applyRunnerReport.js` persists `outcome.output`\\n  (final assistant text) into the stage report and uses it as\\n  `streamedOutput`; it does not restore tool, thinking, usage, or timing\\n  entries. (Exit-code/output tail behavior is retained.)\\n- `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js::/tasks/:id/logs` additionally emits a\\n  `process:stdout` socket event limited to the runner-prefixed text chunk,\\n  so the live tail matches the coarse ingest.\\n\\n### D. UI already has the viewer we need\\n\\n- `frontend/src/components/logs/` contains `LogViewer.jsx`, `adapters.js`,\\n  `logCategories.js`, `logViewerState.js` with category chips, search, density,\\n  timestamps, grouped expandable rows, and follow-scroll. The task surface\\n  calls `useTaskLogs` -> `adaptTaskEntries`.\\n- `shared/toolLogFormat/` contains `summarizeToolStart`, `summarizeToolResult`,\\n  `summarizeUsage`, `summarizePermission`, `summarizePlan`, `stripAnsi`, plus\\n  normalization/truncation helpers. This is the canonical formatter; do not\\n  duplicate it.\\n- Redaction today is environment-variable-name based only:\\n  `api/agent/harnesses/shared/harnessScaffold.js` exports\\n  `SECRET_NAME_PATTERN`, used to drop secret-shaped env vars from child envs.\\n  There is no content/PII redactor for log text; one must be introduced.\\n- Caps: `config.logEntriesMaxCount` defaults to 500 (from schema/tests).\\n  Survey Q4 (\\\"keep everything\\\") conflicts with the current eviction policy and\\n  needs an explicit decision (pagination/archive, not silent truncation).\\n\\n## Principle used throughout\\n\\nMake change easy first (refactors, redaction choke point, structured transport\\nplumbing with no behavior change), then make the change (widen forwarding,\\npersist/stream everything, render everything). Research that decides the shape\\nof the work comes before coding changes.\\n\\n## Phase 0 — Research first (big unknowns; no behavior change)\\n\\n- R1 Runner->backend log path audit (done largely above; finalize exact\\n  client contract): confirm `runner/client.js::logs` payload constraints,\\n  batching, retry, and whether a structured-event upload is viable or requires\\n  a new endpoint/field. detected somewhere (no: only env-name patterns exist);\\n  - choose `logRecord.js`/`logProcessor.js` as the choke point so all sources\\n    (embedded agent, runner ingest, command stages, git/ci) PASS/FAIL (<s>s)` lines and exit semantics —\n *   but driven by Node (`node:child_process`, no shell), so it runs on\n *   Linux, macOS, and Windows with only Node + npm installed. Shells out\n *   only to `npm`/Node/Docker; the two environment-conditional branches\n *   report SKIP instead of failing when their runtime is absent (Security\n *   Script Tests without `bash`, Container Tests without a Docker daemon).\n *   The fast branches share one overlap window; the Canary Tests branch runs\n *   alone afterwards (see splitGatePhases) — same suites, same exit\n *   semantics, but the heaviest branch never shares CPUs with the unit\n *   suites.\n *   The Container Tests branch runs the static Dockerfile/compose assertions\n *   only; the minutes-long live image build/boot tests are opt-in via\n *   `KAINBAIN_CONTAINER_TESTS=live` (direct suite run, not the gate).\n *   The Canary Tests branch (serial Playwright suite on its own scratch\n *   stack, ~7 min) is IN the default gate so `npm test` and\n *   `deploy.sh --prod` run the exact same suites and regressions surface in\n *   the earliest automated stage, not at the merge/deploy gate (the\n *   #KB-0417 incident). Opt out with `--no-canary` or\n *   `KAINBAIN_SKIP_CANARY=1` for fast sanity cycles; `deploy.sh --prod`\n *   passes `--no-canary` to its `final-test-suite` gate and runs the canary\n *   suite as its own blocking `canary-e2e` gate, so nothing runs twice.\n *   Measured gate wall is ~60-70s without canary (the two unit suites alone\n *   are ~160s of CPU work) and ~366-420s with canary (the serial Playwright\n *   suite is minutes long), so CI stages running this gate need an explicit\n *   `timeout` override well above the 60s engine default\n *   (`config.ciTimeoutMs`) — this project's stage sets 1800s. While branches\n *   run the gate emits `▸ started <name>` lines and a `⏳ still running: …`\n *   tick every 30s (`KAINBAIN_GATE_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS`), so a slow branch\n *   never blanks the output (see scripts/lib/run-parallel.mjs).\n *   `run-tests.sh` is a thin shim over this file so `deploy.sh --prod` and\n *   older docs keep working.\n * @example `npm test` => twelve PASS lines (eleven fast branches + Canary Tests), exit 0\n * @example `npm test -- --no-canary` => eleven PASS lines, exit 0\n ***/\n\nimport { spawnSync } from \"node:child_process\";\nimport fs from \"node:fs\";\nimport os from \"node:os\";\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport { fileURLToPath } from \"node:url\";\nimport { npmExecutable, runParallel } from \"./lib/run-parallel.mjs\";\nimport {\n\tcheckDirectoryForDuplicates,\n\tformatViolationsReport,\n} from \"./check-duplicate-settings.mjs\";\n\nconst REPO_ROOT = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), \"..\");\nconst NPM = npmExecutable();\n\n/***\n * MARK: pruneStaleTestDirectories\n * @description Removes abandoned test directories from the temporary folder if\n *   they are older than maximumAgeInMilliseconds (default: 30 minutes). Vitest\n *   test setup files mint isolated temporary roots for each worker process; on\n *   long-running servers with memory-backed tmpfs, accumulated test roots will\n *   otherwise exhaust all available inodes and cause ENOSPC failures during CI.\n * @example pruneStaleTestDirectories({ temporaryDirectoryPath: \"/tmp\", maximumAgeInMilliseconds: 1800000 })\n * @param {Object} [options]\n * @param {string} [options.temporaryDirectoryPath] - path to inspect, defaults to os.tmpdir().\n * @param {number} [options.maximumAgeInMilliseconds] - cutoff age, defaults to 30 minutes.\n * @returns {number} count of pruned directories\n ***/\nexport function pruneStaleTestDirectories({\n\ttemporaryDirectoryPath = os.tmpdir(),\n\tmaximumAgeInMilliseconds = 30 * 60 * 1000,\n} = {}) {\n\tlet prunedDirectoryCount = 0;\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst directoryEntries = fs.readdirSync(temporaryDirectoryPath, { withFileTypes: true });\n\t\tconst currentTimestamp = Date.now();\n\t\tconst testDirectoryPrefixes = [\n\t\t\t\"kainbain-test-\",\n\t\t\t\"kb-\",\n\t\t\t\"survey-\",\n\t\t\t\"sitedocs-\",\n\t\t];\n\n\t\tfor (const entry of directoryEntries) {\n\t\t\tif (!entry.isDirectory()) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tconst matchesTestPrefix = testDirectoryPrefixes.some((prefix) => entry.name.startsWith(prefix));\n\t\t\tif (!matchesTestPrefix) {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue;\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tconst entryFullPath = path.join(temporaryDirectoryPath, entry.name);\n\t\t\ttry {\n\t\t\t\tconst entryStatistics = fs.statSync(entryFullPath);\n\t\t\t\tconst entryAgeInMilliseconds = currentTimestamp - entryStatistics.mtimeMs;\n\t\t\t\tif (entryAgeInMilliseconds > maximumAgeInMilliseconds) {\n\t\t\t\t\tfs.rmSync(entryFullPath, { recursive: true, force: true });\n\t\t\t\t\tprunedDirectoryCount += 1;\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t} catch {\n\t\t\t\t// Ignore permission errors or concurrent deletion races\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t} catch {\n\t\t// Ignore readdir failures if temporary directory is unreadable\n\t}\n\treturn prunedDirectoryCount;\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: ensureCompileCache\n * @description Defaults `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` (persisted V8 compilation output\n *   the many vitest workers share) and creates the directory, matching the\n *   old shell gate. Children inherit it through `spawn` env.\n * @example ensureCompileCache() => process.env.NODE_COMPILE_CACHE is set\n ***/\nfunction ensureCompileCache() {\n\tif (!process.env.NODE_COMPILE_CACHE) {\n\t\tprocess.env.NODE_COMPILE_CACHE = path.join(os.tmpdir(), \"kainbain-compile-cache\");\n\t}\n\tfs.mkdirSync(process.env.NODE_COMPILE_CACHE, { recursive: true });\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: bashAvailable\n * @description Whether `bash` resolves on PATH (needed only by the\n *   bash-only security-scan harness branch).\n * @example bashAvailable() => true\n * @returns {boolean}\n ***/\nfunction bashAvailable() {\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst result = spawnSync(\"bash\", [\"--version\"], { stdio: \"ignore\", windowsHide: true });\n\t\treturn !result.error;\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn false;\n\t}\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: dockerAvailable\n * @description Whether a Docker daemon is reachable (needed only by the\n *   Container Tests branch, which builds and boots the production image).\n * @example dockerAvailable() => true\n * @returns {boolean}\n ***/\nfunction dockerAvailable() {\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst result = spawnSync(\"docker\", [\"info\"], { stdio: \"ignore\", windowsHide: true });\n\t\treturn !result.error && result.status === 0;\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn false;\n\t}\n}\n\n/***\n * MARK: depcheckAvailable\n * @description Whether the `depcheck` devDependency binary is installed in\n *   the root tree (needed only by the Dependency Check branch). A pure file\n *   probe — no spawn, no network — so it stays fast and offline-safe; a\n *   production-only (`--omit=dev`) provisioning simply reports false and\n *   the gate SKIPs the branch instead of failing it.\n * @example depcheckAvailable() => true\n * @param {Object} [opts]\n * @param {string} [opts.root] - repo root to probe, defaults to the gate's root.\n * @param {string} [opts.targetPlatform] - defaults to process.platform.\n * @returns {boolean}\n ***/\nexport function depcheckAvailable({ root = REPO_ROOT, targetPlatform = process.platform } = {}) {\n\tconst bin = targetPlatform === \"win32\" ? \"depcheck.cmd\" : \"depcheck\";\n\ttry {\n\t\treturn fs.existsSync(path.join(root, \"node_modules\", \".bin\", bin));\n\t} catch {\n\t\treturn false;\n\t}\n}\n\n/***\n✓ 5ms","isError":false,"durationMs":19,"source":"runner-structured","runnerId":"local-alpha","executionId":"a673c8ab-6ef6-4541-9b7c-2406e57ab747","seq":116},"fidelity":"normalized","seq":183,"blockId":"b52","tool":{"callId":"call_fnkwki9s","name":"bash","args":{"command":"cd /home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-2b2c7858-604c-42dc-8a16-6b0f97210a3a && sed -n '1,180p' scripts/run-tests.mjs"},"result":"#!/usr/bin/env node\n/***\n * MARK: run-tests.mjs\n * @description Cross-platform full-project verification gate: the same seven\n *   checks the old `run-tests.sh` ran plus the Container Tests branch, the\n *   Frontend Build branch (exercises the deprecation gate), and the\n *   Dependency Audit Gate, in a single overlap window (the two unit suites\n *   alone take ~2x35s sequentially, so overlapping keeps the wall near one\n *   suite), with identical `Running <name>... agent-style commits on the task branch → open the PR review page → the\n *   file list/diff renders → add a per-line comment → Fail the stage\n *   (feedback pre-filled from the comment) → assert {\n\t\t\t\t\treturn false;\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\treturn !fs.existsSync(path.join(repoDir, \".git\", \"index.lock\"));\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t\t{ timeout: 15000 },\n\t\t)\n\t\t.toBe(true);\n}\n\n/***\n * Enters {\n\t\tgit(repoDir, [\"checkout\", \"-b\", branch]);\n\t} catch {\n\t\tgit(repoDir, [\"checkout\", branch]);\n\t}\n}\n\nasync function createTask(request, { title, goal }) {\n\treturn page.request.get(\n\t\t`${API_BASE}/projects/${project.id}/tasks/${taskId}/review?projectId=${project.id}`,\n\t);\n\texpect(res.ok()).toBeTruthy();\n\treturn Agent Logs to the UI (Runner Parity with Muse Code)\n2|\n3|## Goal\n4|\n5|Restore the pre-runner (monolith) log experience now that agent execution has\n6|moved to out-of-process runners. The UI should feel like watching Muse Code work\n7|live, step by step, with full detail available as searchable history. This is a\n8|log-fidelity and transport parity task, not a product change: no new AI\n9|summaries, reuse existing structured log machinery.\n10|\n11|## Success Criteria (from the survey)\n12|\n13|- Live, step-by-step viewing of an agent running (Q1).\n14|- Always visible, using only data that already exists (Q2 + note \"don't use AI to generate summaries\"):\n15|  - short status updates,\n16|  - actions taken (files read/changed, commands run),\n17|  - full command/tool results,\n18|  - errors and retries,\n19|  - per-step timings.\n20|- The same detail available live and as history (Q3), i.e. full transparency.\n21|- Long-term retention, and the log must be searchable (Q4).\n22|- Secrets and PII are removed automatically before display, persistence, and any commit (Q5), because logs may land in the repository.\n23|- Existing gates stay green: `npm run test:unit`, `npm run lint`, focused log suites and headless screenshot checks.\n24|\n25|## Survey Constraints (binding)\n26|\n27|Taken from `SURVEY.md`:\n28|\n29|- Q1: \"Like watching it work live, step by step (Muse Code style)\".\n30|- Q2: all five detail classes; \"Only use things that already exist, don't use AI to generate summaries\".\n31|- Q3: \"Both live and history\" (\"Full transparency\").\n32|- Q4: \"Keep everything and make it searchable\".\n33|- Q5: \"Yes, hide secrets automatically\" plus PII, so committed logs stay safe.\n34|\n35|## Current-State Evidence (why fidelity was lost)\n36|\n37|### A. The structured pipeline already exists in-process\n38|\n39|- Normalized agent events are defined in `api/agent/sessionEvents.js` as\n40|  `AGENT_EVENT_NAMES`:\n41|  `run_started`, `assistant_delta`, `message_started`,\n42|  `tool_started`, `tool_updated`, `tool_finished`,\n43|  `run_finished`, `run_error`,\n44|  plus unified-log events\n45|  `usage_updated`, `session_meta`, `permission_requested`,\n46|  `permission_resolved`, `plan_updated`, `reasoning_delta`,\n47|  `harness_log`.\n48|- `api/agent/logStream/logProcessor.js` turns those events into canonical,\n49|  grouped records over feeds `main`, `thinking`, `tools`, `telemetry`, `raw`.\n50|- `api/agent/logStream/agentLogStreamer.js` wraps the processor and exposes\n51|  `handleEvent`, `system`, `consumeFeed`, `snapshot`, `renderText`,\n52|  `renderFeed`; `agentRunner.js` uses it in the embedded path and passes\n53|  entries through `onChunk`.\n54|- `api/watch/processLogs.js` renders legacy tags from structured entries,\n55|  synthesizes entries for system/GIT/CI/RUNNER lines, manages entry caps\n56|  (`_appendProcessLog`, `_appendLogEntries`, `_replaceLogEntries`,\n57|  `_capLogEntries`), and maps runner frames to kind `runner`.\n58|\n59|### B. The embedded path already preserves this\n60|\n61|In `api/flow/execution/executeStage.js` (embedded mode), `agentRunner(...)`\n62|receives `onChunk`; each chunk (`entry.text`) is appended via\n63|`_appendProcessLog` while running, and after the stage\n64|`_replaceLogEntries(task, startIndex, result.logEntries)` upgrades the\n65|synthesized entries to the streamer's structured entries. The candidate\n66|UI then receives everything through `adaptTaskEntries` in\n67|`frontend/src/components/tasks/LogsPanel.jsx` -> `LogViewer`.\n68|\n69|### C. The runner boundary only carries text — this is the regression\n70|\n71|- `runner/harness.js::runHarnessStage` subscribes to the session but forwards\n72|  only:\n73|  - `assistant_delta.delta` as `event.delta`\n74|  - `harness_log.text` as `event.text`,\n75|  and only those two. It drops `tool_started/updated/finished` (args, full\n76|  results, timings), `reasoning_delta`, `usage_updated`, `permission_*`,\n77|  `plan_updated`, and structured error/retry data. It returns only `output`.\n78|- `runner/daemon.js` turns any `onLog(text)` call into newline-split chunks via\n79|  `sendLogs`, each POSTed to `/tasks/:id/logs` with `bytes` only.\n80|- `api/flow/executionLedger.js::ingestLogs` treats each frame as a text string\n81|  and calls `_appendProcessLog(task, \\`[runner ${runnerId}] ${bytes}\\`, ...)`.\n82|  That is why the UI only sees runner-prefixed text chunks instead of\n83|  `[TOOL]`/`[RESULT]`/`[THINKING]`/telemetry records with args and timings.\n84|- `api/flow/execution/applyRunnerReport.js` persists `outcome.output`\n85|  (final assistant text) into the stage report and uses it as\n86|  `streamedOutput`; it does not restore tool, thinking, usage, or timing\n87|  entries. (Exit-code/output tail behavior is retained.)\n88|- `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js::/tasks/:id/logs` additionally emits a\n89|  `process:stdout` socket event limited to the runner-prefixed text chunk,\n90|  so the live tail matches the coarse ingest.\n91|\n92|### D. UI already has the viewer we need\n93|\n94|- `frontend/src/components/logs/` contains `LogViewer.jsx`, `adapters.js`,\n95|  `logCategories.js`, `logViewerState.js` with category chips, search, density,\n96|  timestamps, grouped expandable rows, and follow-scroll. The task surface\n97|  calls `useTaskLogs` -> `adaptTaskEntries`.\n98|- `shared/toolLogFormat/` contains `summarizeToolStart`, `summarizeToolResult`,\n99|  `summarizeUsage`, `summarizePermission`, `summarizePlan`, `stripAnsi`, plus\n100|  normalization/truncation helpers. This is the canonical formatter; do not\n101|  duplicate it.\n102|- Redaction today is environment-variable-name based only:\n103|  `api/agent/harnesses/shared/harnessScaffold.js` exports\n104|  `SECRET_NAME_PATTERN`, used to drop secret-shaped env vars from child envs.\n105|  There is no content/PII redactor for log text; one must be introduced.\n106|- Caps: `config.logEntriesMaxCount` defaults to 500 (from schema/tests).\n107|  Survey Q4 (\"keep everything\") conflicts with the current eviction policy and\n108|  needs an explicit decision (pagination/archive, not silent truncation).\n109|\n110|## Principle used throughout\n111|\n112|Make change easy first (refactors, redaction choke point, structured transport\n113|plumbing with no behavior change), then make the change (widen forwarding,\n114|persist/stream everything, render everything). Research that decides the shape\n115|of the work comes before coding changes.\n116|\n117|## Phase 0 — Research first (big unknowns; no behavior change)\n118|\n119|- R1 Runner->backend log path audit (done largely above; finalize exact\n120|  client contract): confirm `runner/client.js::logs` payload constraints,\n121|  batching, retry, and whether a structured-event upload is viable or requires\n122|  a new endpoint/field. Output: event-coverage matrix with rows = 17\n123|  normalized AGENT_EVENT_NAMES and runner columns `forward`,\n124|  `preserve order`, `backend ingest`, `live socket`, `persisted`,\n125|  `UI render`; mark current-state pass/drop, and the target state every row\n126|  must reach.\n127|- R2 Backend->UI/live path audit: map `api/routes/ws.js`, `api/eventBridge.js`,\n128|  `api/routes/sessions.js`, task log endpoints, `useWebSocket`, `useTaskLogs`,\n129|  `adaptTaskEntries`, `fullTextIndex`, and `normalizeEntries`. Confirm (a)\n130|  whether WS delivers structured entries or only process lines, (b) what the\n131|  logs tab refetches after run completion, and (c) how history is retained\n132|  and capped. Output: second half of coverage matrix + retention limits.\n133|- R3 Redaction inventory and chosen home:\n134|  - reuse `SECRET_NAME_PATTERN` for env-var-name secrets;\n135|  - add a content redactor for tokens, keys, passwords, bearer/basic\n136|    headers, connection strings, cloud credential JSON, PII (emails, user\n137|    paths, phone/card-like), with evidence on whether each category is\n138|    already detected somewhere (no: only env-name patterns exist);\n139|  - choose `logRecord.js`/`logProcessor.js` as the choke point so all sources\n140|    (embedded agent, runner ingest, command stages, git/ci) share one\n141|    redactor, and document allow-list assumptions.\n142|- R4 Retention and search feasibility:\n143|  - evaluate `logEntriesMaxCount`/lane budgets against \"keep everything\";\n144|  - propose retention model: raised cap + bounded lane budgets, client-side\n145|    full-text search retained, with optional paged history beyond cap via\n146|    execution-archive only if volume demands;\n147|  - keep the eviction marker contract intact.\n148|- R5 (small) confirmation of runner UI category wiring: inspect whether the\n149|  smoothness issue is caused only by coarse runner chunks, or additionally by\n150|  monitor surfaces that exclude tool mirrors. Output: call sites and chips.\n151|- Gate: append the finalized coverage matrix + decisions to this file before\n152|  changing behavior. If R1-R4 contradict the plan below, revise first.\n153|\n154|## Phase 1 — Make the change easy (refactors, no behavior change)\n155|\n156|- E1 Freeze the parity contract.\n157|  - Add/extend a contract test in `api/agent/logStream/harnessFidelity.test.js`\n158|    (or sibling) that asserts every `AGENT_EVENT_NAMES` entry maps to a\n159|    structured record + feed + rendered tag, and captures failing rows as the\n160|    acceptance checklist. No producer change yet.\n161|- E2 Single redaction choke point.\n162|  - Introduce one redaction helper (new module under `shared/` or `api/watch/`\n163|    per R3, no duplication), applied inside `logRecord.js`/`logProcessor.js`\n164|    at record creation, and inside runner ingest and `applyRunnerReport` for\n165|    any text passed through.\n166|  - Wire into the embedded path; verify byte-identical behavior on clean\n167|    inputs (all existing tests green) by covering redaction fixtures.\n168|- E3 Runner plumbing for structured events without changing current behavior.\n169|  - Refactor `runHarnessStage` subscription to an `onEvent(event)` structured\n170|    callback, deriving `onLog(text)` for backwards compatibility. Add\n171|    optional structured upload hooks, keeping existing text behavior as a\n172|    fallback.\n173|  - Unit-test that existing callers receive byte-identical text output.\n174|- E4 Structured ingest in backend, optional and backward-compatible.\n175|  - Extend `/tasks/:id/logs` or add `/tasks/:id/log-events` (R1 decision) so a\n176|    runner can send structured event batches; `executionLedger` forwards them\n177|    to `_appendLogEntries`/`_replaceLogEntries`-style handling, preserves seq\n178|    ordering and gap/duplicate semantics, while still falling back to prefixed\n179|    text for old runners.\n180|\n181|## Phase 2 — Make the change (restore fidelity)\n182|\n183|- C1 Runner forwards everything.\n184|  - Change `runHarnessStage` and daemon sending to forward all normalized\n185|    events with payload (tool args, tool result partials/finals, thinking\n186|    deltas, usage, permissions, plan updates, session meta, errors/retries)\n187|    and timing data derived from event processing.\n188|  - Preserve runner-generated `seq` ordering across batches and retries.\n189|  - Redact on the sending side too, in case a runner runs locally and reads\n190|    local secret-bearing output.\n191|- C2 Backend persists and streams everything.\n192|  - Route runner events through `agentLogStreamer`/`logProcessor` (or the same\n193|    structured ingest path as E4) into `task.logEntries`.\n194|  - Raise/justify retention caps per R4; never silently drop events except\n195|    under the existing eviction marker.\n196|  - Push the same events to live WS channel with structured entry shape, not\n197|    only the `[runner ...]` text line; keep that text line as one legacy view.\n198|  - Ensure `applyRunnerReport` receives/stores structured `logEntries`\n199|    (or preserves the ingested ones) and passes final output separately.\n200|- C3 UI renders everything live and as history.\n201|  - Ensure `adaptTaskEntry` and `adaptProcessLogLine` preserve tags/kind/tool\n202|    fields, timing fields, and expandable detail.\n203|  - Add/enable categories for tool arguments, tool results, thinking,\n204|    errors/retries, permissions, plan updates, telemetry, raw evidence in\n205|    `LogViewer`.\n206|  - Live append must remain incremental with follow-scroll; follow-scroll\n207|    restoration on tab return must still work.\n208|  - History view must refetch complete retained log and keep client-side\n209|    searching; confirm search finds tool names, command names, error text.\n210|- C4 \"Keep everything, searchable\" + secret/PII safety.\n211|  - Implement R4 retention (cap changes + lane budgets + pagination/virtual\n212|    scroll if needed), keeping eviction markers for units beyond cap.\n213|  - Add test proving a secret in a tool result never reaches `task.logEntries`,\n214|    live WS payload, task docs committed, or report persisted output tail.\n215|  - Cover PII shape fixtures from R3.\n216|\n217|## Phase 3 — Assurance (testing + documentation)\n218|\n219|- T1 Contract + unit tests (primary gate `npm run test:unit`):\n220|  - parity contract from E1 fully green;\n221|  - redaction tests for env-name secrets, Inline key/value, bearer/basic,\n222|    connection strings, cloud credentials, PII (email/user path/phone/card)\n223|    plus clean-input passthrough;\n224|  - runner forwarding/ordering tests;\n225|  - executionLedger structured ingest tests including seq gaps/duplicates;\n226|  - adapter/category tests for every feed/kind.\n227|- T2 Integration tests:\n228|  - runner->backend->WS round-trip asserting a tool call with args/result,\n229|    an error/retry, and a timing record arrive live and persist as history;\n230|  - history fetch/search across completed runs;\n231|  - applyRunnerReport keeps structured entries and report detail.\n232|- T3 UI verification:\n233|  - use existing `LogViewer` unit tests + fixture data for all categories,\n234|    timestamps, density, search, expand/collapse, follow-scroll;\n235|  - visual only via `npm run capture:screenshot` against existing\n236|    fixtures/mocks if needed; no bespoke long-lived servers.\n237|- T4 Gates before completion:\n238|  - `npm run test:unit` (must pass),\n239|  - `npm run lint` (must pass),\n240|  - `npm run docs:check` if documentation content is changed.\n241|  Record commands and results in the stage/final report.\n242|- D1 Documentation:\n243|  - short section describing what is logged, live/history behavior, retention\n244|    and search, redaction guarantee, ordering/gap behavior, and residual\n245|    unknown-secret risk (report-a-secret path);\n246|  - keep it linked from existing task/activity docs rather than duplicating\n247|    contract text.\n248|- D2 Appendix:\n249|  - final coverage matrix with all rows passing;\n250|  - explicit non-goals (no AI summaries, no new transport, no new formatter,\n251|    no server-side full-text search unless R4 proves client-side insufficient).\n252|\n253|## Validation Plan\n254|\n255|- Primary gate: `npm run test:unit`.\n256|- Secondary: `npm run lint`, and `npm run docs:check` once D1 lands.\n257|- Focused suites: `api/agent/logStream/*.test.js`, `api/flow/runnerRoutes.test.js`,\n258|  runner tests, `frontend/src/components/logs/*`.\n259|- Manual/headless: open a task using a mock log fixture and verify\n260|  step-by-step live appends (assistant text, assistant reasoning, tool call\n261|  with args, tool result, error/retry, usage, permission/plan), timings, then\n262|  reload and confirm identical history, search for a tool name, and confirm a\n263|  secret/PII is absent from store/WS/report via tests. Use\n264|  `npm run capture:screenshot` only if a visual concern remains.\n265|\n266|## Risks and Mitigations\n267|\n268|- Volume vs. \"keep everything\": mitigate with pagination/virtual scroll and\n269|  lane budgets, not narrative truncation.\n270|- Ordering across runner->backend->WS and retries: pin a seq/timestamp\n271|  contract in the new structured ingest and integration-test it.\n272|- Unknown secret shapes: redactor starts from R3 inventory + common patterns;\n273|  document residual risk and report-a-secret path.\n274|- Secret-safe by position: redact before persistence and before commits;\n275|  tests cover store, WS, and report paths.\n276|- Backwards compatibility: text ingest (`/tasks/:id/logs`) remains usable,\n277|  so older runners degrade only to the current coarse text view rather than\n278|  failure.\n279|\n280|## Phase 0 Findings (research gate — completed before behavior changes)\n281|\n282|- R1 Runner->backend contract: `runner/client.js::logs` posts `{seq, bytes}`;\n283|  structured transport added as `POST /tasks/:id/log-events` with\n284|  `{seq, events[1..200]}` (400 otherwise). Batches retry-safe via the same\n285|  seq gap/duplicate semantics as text frames.\n286|- R2 Backend->UI path: `process:stdout` WS -> `addProcessLog` ->\n287|  `wsProcessLogs` -> `normalizeEntries` (dedupes on `executionId:seq`) ->\n288|  `adaptTaskEntries` -> LogViewer. Structured batches ride a new\n289|  `process:log-entries`/`PROCESS_LOG_ENTRIES` frame into the same array as\n290|  attached `.entry` records, so stored/live dedupe is unchanged. After a\n291|  run the Logs tab refetches `task.logEntries` (identical records).\n292|- R3 Redaction home: new `shared/redactSecrets.js` (superset of the old\n293|  `scrubSecrets` raw-lane patterns) applied at record creation in\n294|  `logProcessor.appendRecord` (text + meta/tool/usage/evidence, plus\n295|  post-creation `meta.output`/partial appends redacted at extraction),\n296|  in `processLogs._synthesizedLogEntry`, in `executionLedger` ingest, in\n297|  the runner sender before upload, and on `applyRunnerReport` outputs.\n298|  `SECRET_NAME_PATTERN` stays the child-env seam; `SECRET_KEY_PATTERN`\n299|  extends it to structured payload keys.\n300|- R4 Retention: `logEntriesMaxCount` default 500 KEPT (not raised) — the\n301|  cap bounds the live/loaded view only; full history persists in committed\n302|  task markdown (`Log Entries`) and stage reports, with eviction markers\n303|  and client-side search over everything retained.\n304|- R5 UI wiring: no new viewer needed — `LogViewer` categories already cover\n305|  tool/thinking/error/permission(`human`)/plan(`stage`)/telemetry+raw(`raw`)/\n306|  runner lanes; search extended to detail + `meta.toolName`. Per-step\n307|  timings had no rendered home: the processor now stamps `durationMs`\n308|  (explicit event timing, else measured >=100ms) and renders it on\n309|  `[RESULT]`/`[ERROR]` lines.\n310|- Correction: the plan says \"17 AGENT_EVENT_NAMES\" — the actual vocabulary\n311|  is 15 (8 original + 7 unified). Pinned by the parity contract test.\n312|\n313|## Appendix — Final Event Coverage (runner boundary, all rows passing)\n314|\n315|| Event | Runner forwards | Backend persisted | Live UI category | Status |\n316|| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n317|| run_started | yes | yes (turn tracking) | system (turn groups) | structured |\n318|| assistant_delta | yes (full text) | yes | output | structured Each category keeps its own marker so a\n20| *   redacted log still tells the reader WHAT kind of value was hidden (a\n21| *   token vs an email vs a home directory) without revealing any of it.\n22| * @example REDACTED.TOKEN => '[REDACTED]'\n23| ***/\n24|export const REDACTED = Object.freeze({\n25|\tSECRET: \"[REDACTED]\",\n26|\tTOKEN: \"[REDACTED]\",\n27|\tEMAIL: \"[REDACTED EMAIL]\",\n28|\tPHONE: \"[REDACTED PHONE]\",\n29|\tCARD: \"[REDACTED CARD]\",\n30|\tPATH: \"[REDACTED]\",\n31|\tKEY: \"[REDACTED PRIVATE KEY]\",\n32|});\n33|\n34|/***\n35| * MARK: redactSecretsText\n36| * @description Redacts secret and PII shapes inside one text value.\n37| *   Non-strings return \"\" (mirrors `stripAnsiText`); clean text returns\n38| *   unchanged (same reference semantics as String.replace with no match —\n39| *   callers can rely on byte-identical output for secret-free inputs).\n40| * @example redactSecretsText('hi') => 'hi'\n41| * @example redactSecretsText('Bearer [REDACTED]') => 'Bearer [REDACTED]'\n42| * @param {string} text - Rendered log text that may carry secrets.\n43| * @returns {string} The text with secret/PII shapes replaced.\n44| ***/\n45|export const redactSecretsText = (text) => {\n46|\tif (typeof text !== \"string\" || !text) return \"\";\n47|\tlet out = text;\n48|\t// Private key blocks first: they span lines and contain base64 that\n49|\t// later patterns would only partially redact.\n50|\tout = out.replace(\n51|\t\t/-----BEGIN [A-Z0-9 ]*PRIVATE KEY-----[\\s\\S]*?-----END [A-Z0-9 ]*PRIVATE KEY-----/g,\n52|\t\tREDACTED.KEY,\n53|\t);\n54|\t// Bearer [REDACTED] Basic [REDACTED] headers.\n55|\tout = out.replace(/(bearer\\s+)[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]{8,}/gi, `$1${REDACTED.SECRET}`);\n56|\tout = out.replace(/(basic\\s+)[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=]{8,}/gi, `$1${REDACTED.SECRET}`);\n57|\t// Vendor token shapes.\n58|\tout = out.replace(/sk-(?:live|test|proj)-[A-Za-z0-9]{8,}/g, \"sk-[REDACTED]\");\n59|\tout = out.replace(/xox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,}/g, \"xox-[REDACTED]\");\n60|\tout = out.replace(/\\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{8,}/g, \"gh_[REDACTED]\");\n61|\tout = out.replace(/AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}/g, \"AIza[REDACTED]\");\n62|\tout = out.replace(/AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}/g, \"AKIA[REDACTED]\");\n63|\t// Connection strings and embedded-credential URLs: keep the scheme so\n64|\t// the reader still knows the backend kind, drop everything secret.\n65|\tout = out.replace(\n66|\t\t/(postgres(?:ql)?|mysql|mongodb(?:\\+srv)?|redis(?:s)?|amqp(?:s)?):\\/\\/[^\\s\"'`]+/gi,\n67|\t\t`$1://${REDACTED.SECRET}`,\n68|\t);\n69|\tout = out.replace(/(\\w+:\\/\\/[^/\\s:]+:)[^@\\s/]+@/g, `$1${REDACTED.SECRET}@`);\n70|\t// AWS-style secret access keys inside JSON credential blobs.\n71|\tout = out.replace(\n72|\t\t/(\"(?:aws_secret|secret_access_key|session_token)\"\\s*:\\s*\")[^\"]*(\")/gi,\n73|\t\t`$1${REDACTED.SECRET}$2`,\n74|\t);\n75|\t// Labeled key/value pairs: api_key=..., \"password\": \"...\", CLIENT_SECRET: ...\n76|\t// The key list mirrors SECRET_NAME_PATTERN plus wire formats (apiKey,\n77|\t// client_secret, authToken). A real `:`/`=` separator is required — bare\n78|\t// prose (\"secret reasoning step one\") must never redact — and the value\n79|\t// needs at least 6 chars so short words after a colon survive.\n80|\tout = out.replace(\n81|\t\t/\\b(api[_-]?key|auth[_-]?token|client[_-]?secret|credential(?:s)?|passwd|password|pwd|secret|token)\\b(\\s*[\"']?\\s*[:=][=>]?\\s*[\"']?)([A-Za-z0-9._~+/=:@-]{6,})/gi,\n82|\t\t`$1$2${REDACTED.SECRET}`,\n83|\t);\n84|\t// ENV-style assignments with secret-shaped names: FOOBAR_API_KEY=[REDACTED]]].\n85|\tout = out.replace(\n86|\t\t/\\b([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*(?:SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|PASSWD|PWD|CREDENTIAL|API[_-]?KEY|PRIVATE[_-]?KEY)[A-Z0-9_]*)\\s*=\\s*(\"[^\"]*\"|'[^']*'|[^\\s,;}\\]]+)/g,\n87|\t\t`$1=${REDACTED.SECRET}`,\n88|\t);\n89|\t// PII: emails, home directories (never /tmp or repo-relative paths),\n90|\t// phone shapes, and spaced/dashed 16-digit card runs.\n91|\tout = out.replace(\n92|\t\t/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/g,\n93|\t\tREDACTED.EMAIL,\n94|\t);\n95|\tout = out.replace(/\\/(home|Users)\\/[^\\s/\"'`:\\n]+/g, `/$1/${REDACTED.PATH}`);\n96|\tout = out.replace(\n97|\t\t/\\b(?:\\+?1[-.\\s]?)?\\(?\\d{3}\\)?[-.\\s]\\d{3}[-.\\s]\\d{4}\\b/g,\n98|\t\tREDACTED.PHONE,\n99|\t);\n100|\tout = out.replace(/\\b\\d{4}[- ]\\d{4}[- ]\\d{4}[- ]\\d{4}\\b/g, REDACTED.CARD);\n101|\treturn out;\n102|};\n103|\n104|/***\n105| * MARK: SECRET_KEY_PATTERN\n106| * @description Secret-shaped object key names (mirrors `SECRET_NAME_PATTERN`\n107| *   in `api/agent/harnesses/shared/harnessScaffold.js`, extended to wire\n108| *   spellings like `apiKey`/`client_secret`). A string value under one of\n109| *   these keys is a secret by position even when the value itself carries no\n110| *   recognizable shape — the same rule the child-env seam already enforces.\n111| * @example SECRET_KEY_PATTERN.test(\"apiKey\") => true\n112| * @example SECRET_KEY_PATTERN.test(\"model\") => false\n113| ***/\n114|export const SECRET_KEY_PATTERN =\n115|\t/secret|token|password|passwd|pwd|credential|api[_-]?key|private[_-]?key|access[_-]?key|client[_-]?secret|auth/i;\n116|\n117|/***\n118| * MARK: redactDeepStrings\n119| * @description Deep-clones a JSON-ish value while redacting every string it\n120| *   contains. Used for structured payloads (tool args/results, permission\n121| *   targets, raw evidence) where a secret may sit in a nested field, not in\n122| *   rendered text. A string under a secret-shaped key (`SECRET_KEY_PATTERN`)\n123| *   is redacted by position even when the value looks innocent; numbers,\n124| *   booleans, null, and undefined pass through untouched (so usage token\n125| *   counts survive); circular values degrade to \"[Unserializable]\" instead of\n126| *   throwing.\n127| * @example redactDeepStrings({ a: 'Bearer [REDACTED]' }) => { a: 'Bearer [REDACTED]' }\n128| * @param {*} value - Any JSON-ish value.\n129| * @returns {*} A redacted deep clone.\n130| ***/\n131|export const redactDeepStrings = (value) => {\n132|\t// Ancestor set only: a reference shared between siblings is cloned twice,\n133|\t// while a true cycle (an object reachable from itself) degrades safely.\n134|\tconst ancestors = new Set();\n135|\tconst walk = (node) => {\n136|\t\tif (typeof node === \"string\") return redactSecretsText(node);\n137|\t\tif (!node || typeof node !== \"object\") return node;\n138|\t\tif (ancestors.has(node)) return \"[Unserializable]\";\n139|\t\tancestors.add(node);\n140|\t\ttry {\n141|\t\t\tif (Array.isArray(node)) return node.map(walk);\n142|\t\t\tconst out = {};\n143|\t\t\tfor (const key of Object.keys(node)) {\n144|\t\t\t\t// eslint-disable-next-line security/detect-object-injection -- key comes from Object.keys of the walked object\n145|\t\t\t\tconst child = node[key];\n146|\t\t\t\tif (typeof child === \"string\" && SECRET_KEY_PATTERN.test(key)) {\n147|\t\t\t\t\t// eslint-disable-next-line security/detect-object-injection -- key comes from Object.keys of the walked object\n148|\t\t\t\t\tout[key] = REDACTED.SECRET;\n149|\t\t\t\t} else {\n150|\t\t\t\t\t// eslint-disable-next-line security/detect-object-injection -- key comes from Object.keys of the walked object\n151|\t\t\t\t\tout[key] = walk(child);\n152|\t\t\t\t}\n153|\t\t\t}\n154|\t\t\treturn out;\n155|\t\t} finally {\n156|\t\t\tancestors.delete(node);\n157|\t\t}\n158|\t};\n159|\treturn walk(value);\n160|};"}},{"id":39,"ts":"2026-11-01T23:48:19.710Z","feed":"main","feeds":["main","tools"],"kind":"tool","turn":1,"text":"[TOOL] bash({\"command\":\"npm test -- --no-canary 2>&1 | tail
