text file `/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-2b2c7858-604c-42dc-8a16-6b0f97210a3a/site-docs/unified-logging.md`.\n1|---\n2|title: Unified Logging\n3|section: how-it-works\n4|order: 75\n5|slug: unified-logging\n6|---\n7|\n8|# Unified Logging\n9|\n10|KainBain captures agent execution as **structured entries** (`task.logEntries`) through a single processing layer so that every harness — Pi, OpenCode, Mistral Vibe, Antigravity, Muse, Custom, and Mock — is observed on the same terms. The full design lives in `docs/EngineDetails/UnifiedLogging.md`.\n11|\n12|## Feeds\n13|\n14|The log viewers expose the feeds:\n15|\n16|- `ALL` — the combined narrative view.\n17|- `ASSISTANT`, `THINKING`, `TOOLS` — the historical feeds.\n18|- `SYSTEM` — engine and harness status lines.\n19|- `TELEMETRY` — usage, token and cost records (never part of copy).\n20|- `RAW` — bounded unmapped-wire evidence for post-mortem.\n21|\n22|## Console\n23|\n24|The filter block (category chips, search, density, timestamps) is collapsed by default on every surface; logs render immediately and the user reveals filters with the `Show filters` toggle. When a non-default filter is active while the block is hidden, a `Filters on` badge appears next to the toggle.\n25|\n26|The main page `ActivityConsole` and the monitor page `LiveConsoleWidget`\n27|share the same dark terminal frame (background, header bar, auto-scroll\n28|toggle) through the `CONSOLE_CHROME` constants in\n29|`frontend/src/components/logs/consoleStyles.js`, so the two consoles stay\n30|visually aligned. Tool cards render an empty body until output arrives —\n31|there is no stuck \"Waiting for output...\" placeholder. The activity drawer\n32|starts collapsed on first visit unless \"Default Expanded\" is checked in\n33|Workspace settings; the collapse/expand choice persists across reloads.\n34|\n35|## Kinds and fidelity\n36|\n37|Entries carry `kind` (`assistant`, `thinking`, `tool`, `error`, `system`,\n38|`telemetry`, `permission`, `plan`, `raw`) plus an optional `fidelity`\n39|(`exact`, `normalized`, `synthesized`) and, for tools and telemetry, typed\n40|`tool`/`usage` records. Legacy entries still read unchanged: new fields are\n41|optional and additive, and the exported `normalizeRecord` helper\n42|(`api/agent/logStream/logRecord.js`) can upgrade a legacy entry to the\n43|canonical shape at read time without rewriting storage.\n44|\n45|## Runner transport (agent log parity)\n46|\n47|Out-of-process Runners ship the same normalized events the embedded path\n48|processes in memory. The harness forwards every session event\n49|(`tool_started/updated/finished` with args and full results, `reasoning_delta`,\n50|`usage_updated`, `permission_*`, `plan_updated`, errors/retries with per-step\n51|timings) to `POST /tasks/:id/log-events` as sequenced batches; the backend\n52|runs each batch through the same log processor, appends the canonical\n53|records to `task.logEntries`, and broadcasts them live over the socket\n54|(`PROCESS_LOG_ENTRIES`). The Logs tab therefore shows the same records live\n55|and as history — what you watch mid-run is what a reload shows, searchable\n56|by text, tool name, and expandable detail.\n57|\n58|- Text frames (`POST /tasks/:id/logs`) stay as the backward-compatible\n59|  fallback: old Runners degrade to the coarse `[runner <id>]` view, and a new\n60|  Runner facing an old backend flips to text after the first failed batch.\n61|- Sequencing survives retries and disconnects: duplicate batches are\n62|  recorded no-ops, gaps land as visible \"frames missing\" markers — never\n63|  silently papered over.\n64|- Secrets and PII are redacted before display, persistence, and any commit:\n65|  every record passes the shared redactor (`shared/redactSecrets.js`) at\n66|  creation — bearer/basic [REDACTED], API keys, vendor tokens, connection\n67|  strings, cloud credential JSON, private keys, emails, home directories,\n68|  phone/card shapes, plus secret-shaped values by key name. The live socket\n69|  is covered too: structured batches fan out from already-redacted stored\n70|  records, and legacy text frames are redacted at the broadcast point in\n71|  `POST /tasks/:id/logs` (older Runners ship raw text on the fallback path).\n72|  If a value that looks secret to you ever appears in a log, treat it as a\n73|  bug and report it: unknown shapes are the documented residual risk.\n74|\n75|## Nothing is silently dropped\n76|\n77|Events a mapper cannot interpret land in the `RAW` feed as a\n78|`kind: \"raw\"` record with `evidence.reason = \"unmapped\"`, with the source\n79|payload scrubbed and capped. Reasonable caps apply per lane.\n80|\n81|## Limits and failure behavior\n82|\n83|- Total entries per stage run are bounded by `logEntriesMaxCount`\n84|  (default 500); overflow evicts oldest-first under one updating\n85|  `[INFO] (N earlier log entries evicted)` marker. The in-memory window is\n86|  intentionally bounded while full history is kept elsewhere: every run's\n87|  records persist into the task's markdown (committed to the repository) and\n88|  the stage reports, so \"keep everything\" holds at the history layer and the\n89|  cap only bounds the live/loaded view. Client-side search runs over\n90|  everything retained.\n91|- Telemetry keeps a reserved budget (`telemetryMaxCount`, default 100) and\n92|  raw evidence its own (`rawMaxCount`, default 50, `rawMaxBytes`, default\n93|  8192 per record).\n94|- Malformed input degrades to defaults instead of throwing; unknown\n95|  feed/kind values fall back to `main`/`system`. Legacy tasks without the\n96|  new fields render exactly as before — storage is never rewritten.\n97|\n98|## Related\n99|\n100|- `#/docs/activity-stream`","isError":false,"source":"runner-structured","runnerId":"local-alpha","executionId":"898d1e5b-106e-4cb1-9fa0-e841ee237bfe","seq":37},"fidelity":"normalized","seq":71,"blockId":"b36","tool":{"callId":"call_01a199871e987276b2d97dc61fd67332","name":"read_file","args":"{\"path\":\"/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-2b2c7858-604c-42dc-8a16-6b0f97210a3a/site-docs/unified-logging.md\"}","result":"Read text file `/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-2b2c7858-604c-42dc-8a16-6b0f97210a3a/site-docs/unified-logging.md`.\n1|---\n2|title: Unified Logging\n3|section: how-it-works\n4|order: 75\n5|slug: unified-logging\n6|---\n7|\n8|# Unified Logging\n9|\n10|KainBain captures agent execution as **structured entries** (`task.logEntries`) through a single processing layer so that every harness — Pi, OpenCode, Mistral Vibe, Antigravity, Muse, Custom, and Mock — is observed on the same terms. The harness forwards every session event\n49|(`tool_started/updated/finished` with args and full results, `reasoning_delta`,\n50|`usage_updated`, `permission_*`, `plan_updated`, errors/retries with per-step\n51|timings) to `POST /tasks/:id/log-events` as sequenced batches; the backend\n52|runs each batch through the same log processor, appends the canonical\n53|records to `task.logEntries`, and broadcasts them live over the socket\n54|(`PROCESS_LOG_ENTRIES`). The Logs tab therefore shows the same records live\n55|and as history — what you watch mid-run is what a reload shows, searchable\n56|by text, tool name, and expandable detail.\n57|\n58|- Text frames (`POST /tasks/:id/logs`) stay as the backward-compatible\n59|  fallback: old Runners degrade to the coarse `[runner <id>]` view, and a new\n60|  Runner facing an old backend flips to text after the first failed batch.\n61|- Sequencing survives retries and disconnects: duplicate batches are\n62|  recorded no-ops, gaps land as visible \"frames missing\" markers — never\n63|  silently papered over.\n64|- Secrets and PII are redacted before display, persistence, and any commit:\n65|  every record passes the shared redactor (`shared/redactSecrets.js`) at\n66|  creation — bearer/basic [REDACTED], API keys, vendor tokens, connection\n67|  strings, cloud credential JSON, private keys, emails, home directories,\n68|  phone/card shapes, plus secret-shaped values by key name. The live socket\n69|  is covered too: structured batches fan out from already-redacted stored\n70|  records, and legacy text frames are redacted at the broadcast point in\n71|  `POST /tasks/:id/logs` (older Runners ship raw text on the fallback path).\n72|  If a value that looks secret to you ever appears in a log, treat it as a\n73|  bug and report it: unknown shapes are the documented residual risk.\n74|\n75|## Nothing is silently dropped\n76|\n77|Events a mapper cannot interpret land in the `RAW` feed as a\n78|`kind: \"raw\"` record with `evidence.reason = \"unmapped\"`, with the source\n79|payload scrubbed and capped. Reasonable caps apply per lane.\n80|\n81|## Limits and failure behavior\n82|\n83|- Total entries per stage run are bounded by `logEntriesMaxCount`\n84|  (default 500); overflow evicts oldest-first under one updating\n85|  `[INFO] (N earlier log entries evicted)` marker. The in-memory window is\n86|  intentionally bounded while full history is kept elsewhere: every run's\n87|  records persist into the task's markdown (committed to the repository) and\n88|  the stage reports, so \"keep everything\" holds at the history layer and the\n89|  cap only bounds the live/loaded view. Client-side search runs over\n90|  everything retained.\n91|- Telemetry keeps a reserved budget (`telemetryMaxCount`, default 100) and\n92|  raw evidence its own (`rawMaxCount`, default 50, `rawMaxBytes`, default\n93|  8192 per record).\n94|- Malformed input degrades to defaults instead of throwing; unknown\n95|  feed/kind values fall back to `main`/`system`. Use the project&apos;s existing framework and\nconventions.\n\nLoading this skill does not mean the current turn asked for the change. While you\nare still investigating — explaining existing behavior, or answering a design\nquestion the user raised — use commands that only read and leave the repository\nunmodified, tests included.\n\n## Scale to the task\n\nSkip the failing-test-first workflow below when the change is tiny and leaves\nprogram logic alone (a typo, a text or style tweak, a config value, or a version\npin), when the work is a throwaway prototype or a standalone one-file script or\npage, when the request adds features to a project you created earlier in this\nsession, or when the user asks for speed or a quick result. A quick direct check\nof the changed behavior is enough there; if you add no maintained test, say so in\nthe report. A report that something already\nbuilt behaves wrongly is a bug fix, even when it comes with feature requests.\n\nBefore a test run that may take more than a minute or two, tell the user in one\nline what runs and why. If you poll it, post a short status line between polls;\nnever poll a long run silently.\n\n## Keep the check with the project\n\nFor a bug fix or behavior change, add or update the smallest maintained test in\nthe repository&apos;s normal test layout that exercises the changed behavior. If a\nspecification makes a reusable suite or test category a deliverable, implement\nthat suite instead of treating it as private verification.\n\nAn inline interpreter command, heredoc, scratch script, temporary-directory\ntest, demo, or manual probe may help diagnose the problem, but it does not\nreplace the maintained test. If the repository\nhas no maintained harness and the request does not require one, disclose when\ndurable coverage would be disproportionate or infeasible and use the narrowest\nhonest verification instead.\n\nOn a later turn, update the maintained test even when the old suite remains\ngreen and the user does not repeat the test request. Cover the new behavior,\nnot merely an unrelated cleanup in the test file.\n\n## Prove the maintained check\n\nObserve the authentic failure before the implementation change when it is safe\nand runnable. Then make the smallest implementation change and run the focused\nmaintained test after the final relevant source or test edit.\n\nDo not weaken or delete a real failing test to obtain green. Fix the product,\nor explain why the test&apos;s expectation is wrong before changing that\nexpectation. Do not repeat an unchanged check solely to collect evidence.\n\nRun a broad or full suite only when the user, a repository gate, or\nproportionate risk requires it, and then once, after the final edit, rather\nthan after each intermediate edit.
